Subject: Geo-data questions — EU anchoring + cross-border backup options (post-call)

Hi Liam / Ana —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and a few clarification asks so we can scope a tailored proposal: 

Summary of requirements we captured on the call:
- Primary requirement: All customer-submitted PHI must remain within the EU for processing and primary storage (data-at-rest and in-transit).
- Secondary/DR requirement: Helix is open to off-site backups stored outside the EU if they are encrypted with customer-managed keys; RPO target ~4 hours, RTO target ~2 hours.
- Logging: Audit logs must be available for 12 months, with the ability to redact or mask PII before logs are exported.
- Evidence: SOC 2 + data flow diagrams will be required for procurement.

Open questions for you (so we give the right architecture and price):
1) For the backups stored outside the EU — can you confirm which data classes are acceptable to leave (metadata only vs. full object backups)?
2) Is Helix comfortable with a warm-standby model pinned to an EU region (short failover time) versus a cold backup strategy?
3) Any procurement constraints around key management (must be in-customer KMS/HSM vs. Redwood-managed with BYOK)?

I attached a short post-call summary with the notes and assumptions. Next steps I propose: technical deep-dive with Dev to validate architecture, followed by a compliance pack we can hand to procurement.

If you can reply with clarifications on the three bullets above, we’ll put together two options (Dedicated EU-pinned + cross-border encrypted backup; and Private/VPC deployment fully EU-contained with on-prem backup middleware).

Thanks,

Priya Natarajan

Subject: Re: Geo-data questions — EU anchoring + cross-border backup options (post-call)

Thanks Priya — quick answers inline below and a few clarifying notes. Appreciated the clear recap.

Inline: 
- Backups: We are comfortable with nightly full backups to a non-EU region provided the backups are:
  * Encrypted with customer-managed keys (we prefer BYOK)
  * Stored immutable for 30 days and then archived if necessary
  * Contain encrypted payloads; metadata-only is acceptable for short-term retention but we prefer full backups for restores.
- Warm vs cold: For our use case (production PHI workload), preferred is EU warm-standby (minimal data movement, faster RTO).
- KMS: Procurement preference is BYOK with HSM-backed KMS (we can provide key lifecycle requirements).

Procurement ask: can you provide a compliance checklist and an indicative cost delta for: 
A) EU Dedicated (pinned) + cross-border encrypted backups to US (BYOK)
B) Private VPC — fully EU-contained (no cross-border backups)

We can set up the next technical call on Tue/Wed next week. Attaching a draft backup policy we use internally to give context.

Best,
Liam
Liam O'Connor

Subject: Re: Geo-data questions — technical options for EU anchoring + backups

Hi team —

Thanks for the details, Liam. A few technical clarifications and options from Redwood’s side to match Helix’s constraints: 

1) EU-anchored primary processing/storage:
   - Option A (Recommended): Dedicated EU pools (customer pinned) — primary model weights, KV caches, and object storage remain in a customer-assigned EU tenancy. This meets EU processing/storage constraints and gives predictable throughput.
   - Option B: Redwood Private (VPC) deployed into your EU region — gives you full control and isolation, suitable if procurement insists on customer-managed networking.

2) Cross-border backups:
   - We support BYOK with HSM integration (we can exchange key-wrapping certificates). Backups can be exported nightly to a US region encrypted under your key. Restore workflow can be automated to your EU tenancy.
   - We can also implement a metadata-only snapshot in EU for 30 days to enable rapid restores without cross-border transfer in some failure modes.

3) Failover model and RPO/RTO:
   - Warm-standby: replicate write-ahead logs and recent KV deltas to an EU warm-standby to achieve ~2 hour RTO in most cases (subject to model size and active session state).
   - Cross-region failover to US: supported as a last-resort failover. When that happens, we can limit processing to non-PHI or token-sampled flows until you enable BYOK-enabled decrypt/restore — we’ll work with you to define policy.

4) Logs and redaction:
   - Built-in redaction pipeline (configurable regex/risk rules) before logs leave the EU tenancy. We retain audit logs for 12 months and can feed HatTip/ELK exports on demand.

5) Evidence & procurement artifacts:
   - I’ll attach a brief architecture sketch and a checklist for SOC 2 artefacts we can share.

Actions I propose from Redwood:
- Deliver a short architecture options doc (Dedicated EU vs Private VPC) with estimated costing.
- Provide a drafted compliance checklist and KMS integration steps for your security team.
